paper_metadata.title: Quantum algorithm for calculating risk contributions in a credit portfolio

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based quantum algorithm for estimating CVaR risk contributions in a credit portfolio using multivariate mean estimation and fixed‑point amplitude amplification. The algorithm has query complexity Õ((σ_max√N_gr)/(ε√p)), achieving a quadratic improvement in accuracy ε compared with classical Monte Carlo complexity Õ((σ_max² log(N_gr/δ))/(ε² p)), although classical scaling in the number of groups N_gr can be better.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum algorithm for estimating CVaR risk contributions of credit-portfolio subgroups using simultaneous multivariate mean estimation and fixed-point amplitude amplification.

algorithm.variant: Quantum simultaneous multiple expected-value estimation for CVaR contributions with fixed-point QAA

hyperparameters.Cmax: upper bound on max group CVaR contribution
hyperparameters.sigma_max: upper bound on max conditional standard deviation
hyperparameters.Emax: upper bound on max group exposure sum

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Standard normal distribution is encoded in amplitudes via an SN state preparation oracle; obligor default indicators are generated by controlled rotations conditioned on discretized normal samples; group losses are computed by arithmetic on binary-encoded fixed-point registers.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate group CVaR contributions C_v^K = E[L_K | L >= v] for K in [Ngr] in a credit portfolio under the Merton model.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection / amplitude amplification on the event L >= v; fixed-point QAA used to amplify the marked subspace.

problem_instance.description: Credit portfolio under the single-factor Merton model, partitioned into Ngr obligor groups; the paper is theoretical and does not report a concrete numerical dataset or market instance.

dataset_specification.description: Portfolio defined by exposures e_k, asset correlations a_k, thresholds z_k, and group partition sizes n_1,...,n_Ngr.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No empirical preprocessing; model-based construction from Merton credit-risk parameters and discretized standard normal sampling.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical query-complexity analysis; no numerical benchmark runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct discretized standard-normal state, compute default probabilities via CDF oracle, and use arithmetic circuits for loss aggregation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure outputs of multivariate mean estimator to obtain approximations of all group CVaR contributions.

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic in epsilon; eO(sqrt(Ngr)/epsilon) vs eO(log(Ngr)/epsilon^2)
speedup_claims.conditions: for CVaR contribution estimation using simultaneous multivariate mean estimation and fixed-point QAA; logarithmic factors hidden
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical benchmark; advantage weakens as Ngr increases; quantum method is not asymptotically better in Ngr.

speedup_claims.factor: O(1/sqrt(p)) dependence in the quantum theorem
speedup_claims.conditions: when estimating conditional expectations on the event L >= v
speedup_claims.caveats: The theorem statement includes p in the complexity through the fixed-point amplitude amplification step.

speedup_claims.conditions: rough comparison after neglecting logarithmic factors
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a rough criterion, not a measured crossover.
This is a back-of-the-envelope estimate, not an experiment.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: ~O(sqrt(Ngr)/epsilon) up to logarithmic factors; more precisely query complexity scales as eO(sqrt(Ngr)/epsilon) and with additional 1/sqrt(p) dependence in the theorem statement.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: eO(log(Ngr)/epsilon^2) for Monte Carlo estimation of all group CVaR contributions; more detailed sample complexity eTheta((sigma_max^2 log(Ngr/delta))/(epsilon^2 p)).

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Quantum advantage expected only when (sigma_max^2)/(epsilon^2 p) >> Ngr (Sec. III.F).
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires fault‑tolerant gate-based quantum computers capable of implementing amplitude-estimation style circuits with arithmetic oracles, controlled rotations, and large registers representing many obligors (Nobl) plus amplitude-preparation circuits for discretized normal distributions.
limiting_factors: Algorithm relies on amplitude estimation and fixed-point amplitude amplification requiring deep fault-tolerant circuits
State preparation of a discretized normal distribution and arithmetic circuits scale with Nobl
Quantum advantage decreases as the number of groups Ngr increases
Only asymptotic query complexity analysis; no resource estimates for practical circuits

notes: No concrete hardware platform, qubit count, circuit depth, or experimental benchmark is reported; the paper is a theoretical algorithm paper. num_qubits and circuit_depth are therefore not specified and remain null.
The algorithm family is amplitude-estimation because the paper explicitly builds on quantum multiple expected-value estimation and fixed-point quantum amplitude amplification.
The paper explicitly analyzes only asymptotic query complexity and does not run simulations or hardware experiments.
Authors state a quadratic speedup in accuracy ε but acknowledge classical scaling in Ngr can be better and provide only theoretical conditions for advantage.
